questions.prompt: With the exception of SELV and PELV, the minimum value of insulation resistance is?

questions.prompt: What is the meaning of this symbol?

options.B: Light which can be covered by thermally insulating material
options.C: Luminaire suitable for mounting on a normally flammable surface

questions.prompt: A consumer unit that has a missing blank plate would contravene?

questions.prompt: For how many hours does emergency lighting need to operate in places of entertainment and for sleeping risk?

questions.prompt: You would perform an insulation resistance test in order to?

options.A: Ensure a circuit will disconnect within the required time
options.B: Prove the continuity of the protective conductor
options.C: Test the correct functioning of the mechanical parts of an RCD
options.D: Verify that there is no breakdown in the insulation of the conductor

questions.explanation: An insulation resistance test checks that conductors are properly insulated from each other and from earth. It is used to find insulation breakdown, not to prove disconnection time or RCD operation.

A.text: Automatic disconnection is verified from the fault path, protective-device characteristic and, where used, RCD performance. Insulation resistance does not measure fault-loop operating time.

B.text: Protective-conductor continuity uses a low-resistance continuity test. Insulation testing instead applies a high DC voltage between conductors to find unwanted leakage paths.

C.text: The RCD test button exercises its mechanism, and an RCD tester measures electrical operation. An insulation tester neither trips nor times the RCD mechanism as its purpose.

D.text: An insulation resistance test checks that conductors are properly insulated from each other and from earth. It is used to find insulation breakdown, not to prove disconnection time or RCD operation.

questions.prompt: When a grey core in harmonised three-core-and-cpc cable is used as neutral, what colour identification should be applied at its terminations?
questions.explanation: A conductor used as neutral must be identified blue at its terminations. In the common lighting convention, the grey core is sleeved blue when used as neutral; brown and black remain line-colour identifications, while red is the old pre-harmonisation line colour.

A.text: Black is a harmonised line-core colour. Leaving a grey neutral identified black would misidentify its function and could lead someone to treat it as live.

B.text: Brown identifies a line conductor. Sleeving the grey neutral brown would state the opposite function and create a dangerous identification error.

C.text: A conductor used as neutral must be identified blue at its terminations. In the common lighting convention, the grey core is sleeved blue when used as neutral; brown and black remain line-colour identifications, while red is the old pre-harmonisation line colour.

D.text: Red is the pre-harmonisation line colour, not the current neutral identification. Neutral conductors are identified blue.

questions.prompt: In a two storey domestic house with three bedrooms, a kitchen with a door and a total floor area of less than 200m² per floor, what is the minimum number of smoke alarms required?
questions.explanation: Approved Document B expects smoke alarms on the escape route of each storey in a dwelling. A two-storey house therefore needs at least two alarms.

A.text: No alarms would provide no automatic warning at all and could not meet the recommended Grade D2, Category LD3 provision for a new dwellinghouse.

B.text: A single alarm cannot provide the minimum circulation-space detection on both storeys. Smoke may accumulate on the unprotected floor before reaching that detector.

C.text: Approved Document B expects smoke alarms on the escape route of each storey in a dwelling. A two-storey house therefore needs at least two alarms.

D.text: Four alarms may follow from a more protective, layout-specific design, but bedroom count does not impose one alarm per bedroom. The minimum in the stated two-storey scenario is one per storey.

questions.prompt: Identify one of the following which would definitely have an area which is classed as a 'special location'?

options.A: Bathroom containing a bath or shower

C.text: Fixed garden wiring remains within Part P's general scope, but a garden is not a special location under the current English notification definition. A new circuit can still make the work notifiable.

questions.prompt: During initial verification, copies of certificates containing all necessary information can be found in?
questions.explanation: The IET On-Site Guide includes examples of certificates and schedules for initial verification. It is the everyday reference for the necessary certificate information.

D.text: The IET On-Site Guide includes examples of certificates and schedules for initial verification. It is the everyday reference for the necessary certificate information.

questions.prompt: Where its purpose is not obvious from its position, a switch installed for permanently connected equipment should be?

options.A: Identified according to the equipment supplied

questions.explanation: The switch is identified by the equipment or function it controls so a user or maintainer can operate the correct device safely. Locking and current rating depend on the application and are not universal 20 A or 32 A requirements.

A.text: The switch is identified by the equipment or function it controls so a user or maintainer can operate the correct device safely. Locking and current rating depend on the application and are not universal 20 A or 32 A requirements.

C.text: There is no blanket 20 A minimum for every appliance switch. Its current, utilization category and duty must suit the actual equipment and circuit.

D.text: A universal 32 A rating would be unnecessary for many fixed loads and could still be inadequate for others. Selection follows the design current and switching duty, not a single preset value.

questions.prompt: A blue core used as a strapper on a two way lighting circuit should be?

options.B: Marked with 2 grooves to indicate line conductors
options.C: Sleeved blue to indicate neutral conductors
options.D: Sleeved brown to indicate line conductors

questions.explanation: A blue core used as a line conductor must be identified brown at its terminations. The sleeving shows that the conductor is live in this application rather than a neutral.

A.text: A written label is not the normal core-identification method inside a lighting accessory. A core used as a line conductor needs the prescribed line-colour identification at its terminations.

B.text: Grooves are not a recognised BS 7671 conductor-identification convention. They could be missed and would not establish the conductor function by the harmonised colour system.

C.text: The strapper cores carry switched line potential; they are not neutral conductors. Blue identification would dangerously suggest that a core is at neutral potential.

D.text: A blue core used as a line conductor must be identified brown at its terminations. The sleeving shows that the conductor is live in this application rather than a neutral.

questions.prompt: One of the requirements for initial verification on a completed installation is that?

options.A: All parts of the installation are correctly selected and erected
options.B: The On Site Guide is referenced to ensure the correct Ze of the circuit
options.C: The completed installation is checked at least twice

B.text: Ze is an external earth-fault-loop value at the origin, not a value for each circuit that can be established merely by looking it up. It is measured or reliably obtained from the distributor.

C.text: BS 7671 specifies the inspections and tests needed to verify compliance, not a rule to repeat the whole process exactly twice. Any doubtful or abnormal result is investigated as necessary.

questions.prompt: When calculating the maximum current demand of a cooker circuit, you can refer to?
questions.explanation: The On-Site Guide gives practical diversity guidance for cooker circuits. It is the reference used to estimate maximum demand rather than simply adding the full appliance rating.

questions.prompt: The minimum distance a fixed data broadband cable should be installed away from 230v services is?

questions.prompt: When supplying remote installations, SWA is often preferred as?

options.C: It is a cheaper method for long cable runs

questions.explanation: SWA cable has steel wire armour that gives strong mechanical protection. That makes it a common choice for remote supplies and buried or exposed runs.

C.text: SWA cable, glands and termination labour can cost more than other suitable systems. Selection is based on the route and risks, not a universal long-run price advantage.

questions.prompt: A 30mA RCD used for additional protection, provides protection against?
questions.explanation: A 30 mA RCD used for additional protection detects residual current leaking from line to earth. It is shock protection, not overload or short-circuit protection.

A.text: A 30 mA RCD used for additional protection detects residual current leaking from line to earth. It is shock protection, not overload or short-circuit protection.

B.text: Current flowing from line to neutral normally returns through the RCD's monitored conductors, so there is no residual imbalance to detect. An overcurrent device deals with a low-impedance line-neutral fault.

C.text: An overload can be perfectly balanced between line and neutral, so a residual-current device may not trip. A fuse, MCB or the overcurrent element of an RCBO provides overload protection.

D.text: A line-neutral short circuit is primarily cleared by overcurrent protection. An RCD responds to residual current escaping the intended live-conductor path and is not a replacement for short-circuit protection.

questions.prompt: The purpose of the Competent Persons Scheme is to?

options.A: Encourage electrical engineers to further their education
options.B: Ensure checks are carried out on persons involved in electrical installation work
options.C: Maintain a register of competent persons, allowing certification of work to pass to registered competent schemes as opposed to directly to building control
options.D: Provide reassurance to customers requesting electrical work

C.text: The Competent Person Scheme provides a route for registered installers to certify domestic work through their scheme rather than applying directly to Building Control. That is the Part P self-certification route.

questions.prompt: A convenient and satisfactory method of fixing a lightweight item to a plasterboard partition wall would be?

questions.prompt: Which of the following titles is fictitious?

options.B: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002
options.C: Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations 1992
options.D: Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998

questions.prompt: Horizontal chases in walls should be no deeper than?
questions.explanation: A horizontal chase should not be deeper than one sixth of the wall leaf thickness. The limit controls how much load-bearing masonry is removed across the wall; 'thickness of a chase' is not the relevant dimension.

questions.prompt: Under EAWR guidance, a person with adequate technical knowledge or experience to prevent electrical danger is described as?

options.A: Able to prove he/she has worked on an identical installation previously
options.D: Registered on a competent persons scheme

questions.explanation: Such a person is described as competent for the work: they have sufficient knowledge or experience to prevent danger and injury. A particular qualification, prior identical job or scheme registration may support competence but is not the definition itself.

questions.prompt: What is the principle purpose of Part F of the Building Regulations?
questions.explanation: Approved Document F is the Building Regulations guidance for ventilation. It covers provision of fresh air and extract ventilation in buildings.

C.text: Energy performance of the building fabric and services is principally Part L. Insulation can interact with airtightness, but it is not Part F's functional subject.

D.text: Approved Document F is the Building Regulations guidance for ventilation. It covers provision of fresh air and extract ventilation in buildings.

questions.prompt: Two core flexible cable to BS EN 50525 has the colours?
questions.explanation: Two-core flexible cable uses brown for line and blue for neutral under harmonised conductor colours. Those colours make polarity clear.

questions.prompt: When performing a safe isolation test and safely locking off the circuit, the key should be kept?

options.A: Close to the consumer unit in case of emergency
options.D: With the person who isolated the circuit

questions.prompt: Which part of the building regulations refers to the conservation of fuel and power?

options.C: Section 701 of the IET Wiring Regulations

questions.prompt: The selection and installation of lighting diffusers which form part of a ceiling are subject to certain requirements of:

options.D: Code of Practice for rafter roofs

questions.explanation: Approved Document B covers fire safety, including how ceiling linings and fittings behave in fire. Lighting diffusers forming part of a ceiling must not undermine that fire performance.

questions.prompt: Energy efficient systems come under the scrutiny of the Building Regulations:
questions.explanation: Energy-efficient systems fall under Part L, conservation of fuel and power. That Part drives efficient lighting, heating controls and energy performance provisions.

questions.prompt: The Building Regulations are divided into:
questions.explanation: England's current technical requirements are grouped under 18 lettered Parts: A-H, J-M and O-T. 'Sections' is the wrong term, and the older total of 14 no longer includes the later Parts.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a term normally used to express the objectives or 'functional requirements' of the Building Regulations:
questions.explanation: Functional requirements in the Building Regulations use terms such as adequate, appropriate and reasonable. "Usual" is not the normal wording for a requirement.

questions.prompt: In a typical small domestic lighting-circuit design, which listed overcurrent protective-device rating is commonly used?
questions.explanation: A 6 A device is commonly used for a small domestic lighting circuit. The final rating must still be selected from cable capacity, installation method, load, fault protection and voltage drop rather than habit alone.

B.text: A 16 A lighting circuit can be designed in suitable circumstances, so the value is not inherently prohibited. It is nevertheless above the common 6 A arrangement described by this typical small domestic example.

C.text: Thirty-two amperes is commonly associated with a ring final socket-outlet circuit. A small lighting circuit has a much lower design current and is not normally protected at that rating.

D.text: A 6 A device is commonly used for a small domestic lighting circuit. The final rating must still be selected from cable capacity, installation method, load, fault protection and voltage drop rather than habit alone.

questions.prompt: What minimum rated duration is normally required for emergency escape lighting in places used for sleeping and in places of entertainment?
questions.explanation: A three-hour duration is normally required for sleeping accommodation and places of entertainment so escape lighting remains available through an extended supply failure and any evacuation or reoccupation process.

A.text: A one-hour system is appropriate only where evacuation follows immediately and the premises will not be reoccupied until the battery has recharged. Sleeping and entertainment uses normally require the longer three-hour provision.

B.text: A three-hour duration is normally required for sleeping accommodation and places of entertainment so escape lighting remains available through an extended supply failure and any evacuation or reoccupation process.

C.text: Five hours is not the standard rated duration selected for this risk category. Specifying extra autonomy may be a project choice, but it is not the normal minimum being tested.

D.text: Eight hours resembles a working-shift or overnight duration rather than the emergency-lighting classification. The system is designed to support escape and relevant post-failure use for three hours, not an entire night.

A.text: Background ventilators, commonly trickle vents, provide a controllable path for continuous air supply to habitable rooms. Extract systems remove air from wet rooms, while heat-recovery supply is part of a mechanical system rather than natural ventilation.

C.text: Mechanical ventilation with heat recovery supplies and extracts air through fans and transfers heat between the airstreams. It does not rely on background ventilators as the defined natural-air inlet method.

D.text: A passive stack uses vertical ducts and buoyancy to extract air from wet rooms. The question asks for the component that admits replacement outdoor air into habitable rooms, which is the background ventilator.

questions.prompt: Does BS 7671 set a fixed numerical maximum for socket-outlets on a properly designed ring final circuit?

options.C: Limited by the protective device rating
options.D: No fixed numerical limit; the circuit must still satisfy all design constraints

questions.explanation: BS 7671 does not set a simple numerical socket limit for a ring final circuit. The design must still meet limits for load, served floor area where the standard arrangement is used, cable capacity, voltage drop and fault protection.

A.text: Ten is not a general BS 7671 maximum. A compliant design can contain fewer or more outlets according to expected demand, circuit layout, conductor capacity, voltage drop and the applicable ring-final rules.

B.text: Twenty is another arbitrary outlet count rather than a Wiring Regulations limit. Simply staying below twenty would not prove that load distribution, floor area or cable protection is satisfactory.

C.text: The protective-device rating constrains current and must coordinate with the conductors, but it does not translate into a fixed socket count. The connected and expected loads, not the number of faceplates alone, determine current demand.

D.text: BS 7671 does not set a simple numerical socket limit for a ring final circuit. The design must still meet limits for load, served floor area where the standard arrangement is used, cable capacity, voltage drop and fault protection.

questions.prompt: BS 7671, Requirements for Electrical Installations, is:

options.D: To be used by supervisors only

questions.explanation: BS 7671 is a non-statutory British Standard. It is not itself an Act or regulation, although following it is a widely recognised way to support compliance with legal electrical-safety duties.

A.text: BS 7671 is a non-statutory British Standard. It is not itself an Act or regulation, although following it is a widely recognised way to support compliance with legal electrical-safety duties.

B.text: BS 7671 does not itself acquire legal force merely through publication. A law, contract or specification can require compliance with it, but the underlying legal duty then comes from that separate instrument.

C.text: Statutory instruments are legislation made under powers granted by an Act. BS 7671 is a consensus technical standard; HSE describes it as non-statutory guidance likely to support compliance with electrical-safety law.

D.text: The standard is used by designers, installers, inspectors, testers and maintainers as well as supervisors. Restricting it to one job role would defeat its installation-wide purpose.

questions.prompt: Which design check is specifically prompted by increasing an instantaneous shower rating from 7 kW to 10 kW?

options.A: The cable cpc will not fail under fault current
options.B: The circuit cable and protective device are adequate for the increased load
options.C: The new unit will provide sufficient flow
options.D: The unit will heat the water sufficiently

questions.explanation: The higher power increases design current, so the cable capacity, protective-device rating, voltage drop and fault protection must be reassessed. Water flow and heating performance do not prove that the electrical circuit is adequate.

A.text: Protective-conductor fault withstand always needs to be adequate, but the change in kilowatt rating directly increases normal design current. That first prompts reassessment of the complete circuit cable and protective-device coordination.

B.text: The higher power increases design current, so the cable capacity, protective-device rating, voltage drop and fault protection must be reassessed. Water flow and heating performance do not prove that the electrical circuit is adequate.

C.text: Water flow depends on the appliance, pressure and plumbing conditions. It is not the electrical circuit-design consequence of raising the connected load from 7 kW to 10 kW.

D.text: Heating performance is an appliance-selection matter and the higher rating generally increases available heating power. The installer must still prove that the existing electrical circuit can safely carry and protect the greater current.

B.text: Part P is the broad legal requirement for reasonable electrical safety in dwellings. The immediate, technically identifiable defect is loss of the enclosure's required degree of protection against access to live parts.

C.text: Section 701 adds requirements for locations containing a bath or shower. A consumer-unit opening breaches basic enclosure protection regardless of whether the unit is near such a location.

D.text: Amendment 1 to the 17th Edition is a superseded edition and is not the name of the enclosure property lost by removing a blank. IP classification expresses the relevant protection against access and ingress.

questions.prompt: What is the core requirement for a member of a self-certification scheme (formerly a competent person scheme)?

options.C: Have been a qualified electrician for at least 5 years
options.D: Have completed a relevant and recognised apprenticeship

questions.explanation: The member must demonstrate competence for the work within the scheme's registered scope and operate the required compliance and certification systems. No rule requires every possible qualification or a fixed number of years in the trade.

A.text: The member must demonstrate competence for the work within the scheme's registered scope and operate the required compliance and certification systems. No rule requires every possible qualification or a fixed number of years in the trade.

B.text: No person can or needs to hold every electrical qualification. Assessment is task- and scope-based: the registrant must demonstrate the knowledge, skills and behaviours relevant to the controlled work being certified.

C.text: Length of service can contribute useful experience but does not by itself demonstrate the mandatory technical competences. The scheme assesses current capability for the registered work categories.

D.text: An apprenticeship is a valuable route into the trade, not the only permitted evidence of competence. Scheme registration depends on meeting the applicable assessment criteria rather than one historical training route.

questions.prompt: When a domestic socket circuit is rewired as an alteration, which Building Regulations principle applies to the completed work?

options.B: Every socket must be fixed with its top edge at 450 mm

questions.explanation: Alteration work must comply with the applicable requirements and must not make the dwelling's compliance more unsatisfactory than before. The 450-1200 mm accessibility guidance is not an automatic demand to relocate every existing accessory during any rewire.

B.text: Fixing every socket with its top at 450 mm would place its centre below that reference level and is not a general alteration rule. Existing-building duties are assessed through the applicable requirements and non-worsening principle.

questions.prompt: An electrical contractor can self-certify notifiable work through which route?

questions.explanation: Registration with an authorised self-certification scheme allows the business to certify qualifying work within its approved scope. Experience alone or informal local-authority permission does not create that route.

C.text: Building control can supervise and certify work through its own route, but an informal permission does not make the contractor a self-certifier. Scheme registration is the defined alternative to advance building-control approval.
